newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga shuts in Snorre, Vigdis oilfields.
newsitem.headline: Saga shuts in Snorre, Vigdis oilfields.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Friday it had shut in the North Sea Snorre and Vigdis fields due to burgeoning storage capacity on the Statfjord and Gullfaks developments.

Snorre pumps crude to Statfjord for final processing, storage and loading on to shuttle tankers. Output from Vigdis is first transported to Snorre for processing and later piped to the Gullfaks A installation for shipping.
North Sea loadings have been severely disrupted recently due to hurricane-force winds and high swell.
Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said production had been reduced at Snorre from 1900 GMT on Thursday. Operations were completely shut down at 0400 GMT on Friday.
Snorre produced 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) on Thursday but has a normal capacity of around 230,000 bpd.

Schibevaag said output at the Vigdis field was reduced earlier on Thursday due to problems with the gas compressor. Pumping was completely halted at midnight and the field was not expected to resume production until Sunday, he said.
"Vigdis came onstream in January and we are continuing the tuning process," Schibevaag told Reuters.

Vigdis is planned to produce an average 30,000 bpd but pumped just 12,000 bpd on Thursday, according to Saga's figures. reduced production at the Gullfaks A and Statfjord A and C platforms due to brimming storage tanks, but it expected to begin offshore loadings soon.
Five shuttle tankers were waiting in the area, ready to hook up to the offshore loading buoys when weather conditions permitted.
